name: thermalisation
description: A cloud of hot ions left in a room-temperature gas until it forgets how it was launched. Equipartition then fixes the answer exactly: the mean kinetic energy must be (3/2)kT = 38.778 meV at 300 K, whatever the ions started with. This is the sharpest check the event-driven collision models have, because the closed form is not something the engine knows - it tests the scattering kinematics, the Maxwellian draw and the isotropy of the deflection all at once, and getting the centre-of-mass share wrong settles the ions at the wrong temperature. Launched at 5 eV, some 129 times the target, so a run that merely failed to heat the ions would not pass.
